and commanded the heralds,
and they proclaimed him king of the East and the West.
And when the Sultan was ordered to depart,
he sought for the Caliph to extend his hand to him.
And when he extended it to him,
he kissed it twice and passed it over his eyes.
And he went out, and they mounted him upon one of the Caliph's horses,
and with great pomp he went to his residence.
And in the year 1309 {OCR?}
of the Greeks [1057-1058 AD],
in the winter season,
three thousand Turks came and entered Melitene,
because its wall had been breached since the time Cyriacus took it from the Arabs.
And after they cast heaps of slain in it,
they tortured the remnant,
that they might show them the hidden treasures.
And many died under tortures,
like Peter the deacon, the scribe and teacher of children.
This man was seized while he was writing a liturgical book (penqitha).
And when he wrote:
"The head of John is like a cluster of grapes which Herodias plucked,"
the Turks seized him.
And they melted pitch {OCR?} and poured it upon his head,
and they placed hot coals in a basin upon his chest.
And when he was close to passing away,
he saw the fire catching onto his feet, and he said:
"Blessed are you, for you have been cleansed!" And his soul departed.
And the Turks were in Melitene for twenty days,
destroying and plundering.
And when they burned it with fire and departed,
a severe winter overtook them near the mountain of the people of Sansan (Sanassoun),
and the Armenians came down,
and killed them all.
And those who were saved from the afflicted city returned to it,
among whom was Joseph the monk,
the one who wrote three metrical discourses on this matter.
Lord John bar Shushan also wrote four metrical discourses on the devastation of Melitene:
two in the meter of Saint Ephrem,
and two in the meter of Saint Balai.
And in this captivity, the monastery of Bar Gagai was destroyed,
and was not inhabited again.
And in the year 450

And Inal (Inaj?) {OCR?}, the commander of the Ghuzz, fled,
and entered the citadel of Mosul.
And the Ma'addites came after him and encamped against Mosul,
and a great famine occurred in it,
until the Ghuzz ate their horses and their mules.
